sentences.span: AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying, which the bank calls simply the "AI put."
sentences.why: BofA's equity derivatives team coins the term directly in this note.

sentences.span: a relatively fixed supply of attention", macro risk "is struggling to compete for attention with the growth potential of AI narratives." AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying
sentences.why: Matches the mechanism, the fixed-attention framing, and the dip-buying conclusion verbatim.

sentences.span: on the tug of war between stocks, bonds
sentences.why: Opinion-shaped framing sentence grounded in genuinely different emphases: Goldman's Pasquariello debates what bonds mean for stocks while BofA frames bonds via the AI put/doom-level lens.

sentences.span: S&P has been mired in a tyrannical range trade around the 7700 level for the past two months... one year ago, the forward P/E of S&P was 23x; today it's 19x
sentences.why: Both the multiple compression and the 7700 range level are stated directly.

sentences.span: the increase in rates vol, which as we have previously pointed out is the key for equities, not the level of rates
sentences.why: The clean, explicitly-attributed statement of this exact rule belongs to Deutsche Bank (Parag Thatte), not Goldman. The only Goldman-adjacent phrasing found ("it's the velocity, not the level" in the Zero Hedge Privorotsky writeup) is the aggregator's own unattributed parenthetical, immediately followed by a BNP Paribas quote asserting a specific level (5.5%) does matter — the opposite of "not the level." Attributing this rule to Goldman misstates who said it.

sentences.span: I need rates to calm, credit to stop widening and a more definitive energy solution before taking nets up here
sentences.why: Privorotsky's three-item checklist is quoted directly and matches the sentence's three conditions.

sentences.span: Perhaps this week is the first sign of cracks appearing - Europe might not be able to sustain these levels of rates and funding when growth is just ~1%
sentences.why: Goldman's Macro Roadmap names France/Europe explicitly as where the rates move is breaking something.

sentences.span: Fair value for the 10y OAT-Bund spread stands at 100-110bp... We cut our French growth forecasts again, to 0.3% and 0.6% for this year and next
sentences.why: BofA Global Research states both figures directly and exactly.

sentences.span: The US-centric AI capex cycle is pushing the cost of capital higher globally... does Europe reap enough of the benefits from a growth perspective to be fine too?... growth is just ~1%
sentences.why: Goldman (Codacci-Pisanelli) poses exactly this question with the ~1% growth figure.

sentences.span: 2026 projected hyperscaler issuance of $250bn... most of this year's funding ($230bn) completed. 2027 Hyperscaler forecasts of $420bn of gross issuance... (vs. $400bn...) 35% of 2027's hyperscaler CapEx spending will be debt funded
sentences.why: Every figure (250bn, 230bn, 420bn vs 400bn, 35%) matches Goldman's credit desk note exactly.

sentences.span: The junkiest junk is leading credit losses but the rest of high yield is starting to catch up
sentences.why: Directly describes stress concentrated at the bottom of the credit stack (CCC-rated).

sentences.span: Oracle matters here purely as a credit story. Its 5Y CDS hit a record ~227 bps, its 2056 bonds yield above 8%... CCCs hit 1,007 bps, the first time above 1,000 since the March 2023 bank scare
sentences.why: Every figure (1,007bp, March 2023, Oracle 227bp CDS, 2056 bonds above 8%) matches exactly.

sentences.span: I need rates to calm, credit to stop widening and a more definitive energy solution before taking nets up here
sentences.why: Goldman's actual named condition is a three-item checklist (rates calm, credit stop widening, energy resolution), not "a reversal in real yields." BofA's framing ("Stuck in a 5% World") names nominal yield levels (5%/6%/7% doom levels) as the thing that matters, not a real-yields reversal either. No source has either desk naming "a reversal in real yields" as the shared trigger; the sentence manufactures a specific convergence between the two banks that the source texts do not state.

sentences.span: Oil prices extended the week's rise, with Brent above $102 by late Friday
sentences.why: Brent level/timing matches exactly; the Persian Gulf exports figure (23.6mb/d, just above 2025 average, roughly balanced market) matches Goldman's Daan Struyven in a companion file (18660__gs-crook-connecting-you-to-gs-thoughts-from-the-floor-3-oct-.txt: "recovered to 23.6mb/d over the last week or just above their 2025 average" / "global oil market appears roughly balanced").
